source_read: https://viewthe.menu/hwyv (All Day), hwdv (Breakfast), hwuv (Afternoon Tea), hw2v (Petit Pierre), hw7v (Bar Pierre), downloaded fresh 2026-10-08 (robots.txt allows; one request per page), then re-read in headless Chromium (DOM, 'View nutrition information' revealed) and by a separate regex parse
notes: A fresh build from the fresh pages was byte-identical to data/source. Independent parse (not the script's): all 116 published items matched on name + kcal; the Contains and May contain lines of all 116 matched the published allergen keys (cereal / nut kinds checked by eye on the 12 sampled rows incl. French Afternoon Tea, Pain au Chocolat, Traditional Breakfast); vegetarian tags match the page's Vegetarian/Vegan ticks (French BLT Salad deliberately untagged: its description names bacon). Fixed: the Ten Kites helper drops what a dish already contains from may-contain, so policy 2 (name no cereal/nut kinds when the page prints both a contains and a may-contain of the same key) never fired; bistrot_pierre.py now passes the page's raw may-contain keys, so 12 allergen rows (e.g. chicken-supreme-schnitzel, miso-caramel-banana-crepe, beef-burger) now publish generic gluten/nuts without kinds. Held back after checking descriptions against allergens: Houmous (haricot blanc houmous with no sesame mark while the Petit Pierre page marks sesame for the same houmous) and Lamb Tagine ('mint yoghurt' but no milk mark). The earlier audit flag (Houmous name-implies-sesame) is resolved by the hold-back. Dark Chocolate Mousse (no eggs marked) and the gluten-free bread board were considered and kept (no clear contradiction). Calories-only chain: no other nutrient is published.
